description: This line plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC, in percent) of six different methods—Base, MEND, FT, MEMIT, IKE, and ROME—as a function of the co-occurrence number, which is plotted on the x-axis using a logarithmic scale ranging from 0 to 10³ (1000), with tick labels at 0, 10¹ (10), 10² (100), and 10³ (1000). The y-axis represents ACC (%) on a linear scale from 60 to 80. The Base method is shown as a black line with solid circles, starting at approximately 61% and rising to about 66%. The MEND method is depicted as a brown line with diamond markers, beginning at roughly 66% and increasing to approximately 74%. The FT method is a blue line with triangle markers, starting at about 62% and ending near 68%. The MEMIT method is a purple line with circle markers, beginning at approximately 66% and rising to about 72%. The IKE method is a red line with triangle markers, starting at around 65% and ending near 70%. The ROME method is a green line with square markers, beginning at approximately 72% and remaining nearly constant at about 77% across the entire range of the x-axis.
